data.long_meaning: The name Uzielen is of Hebrew origin and is composed of two parts. The first part 'Uzi' means 'my strength' or 'my help'. The second part 'El' is the Hebrew name for God. In Christianity, Uzielen represents the strength and help that comes from God. The name Uzielen carries the meaning “My strength is God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Uzielen usually hope their child will grow to embody my strength is god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Uziel is believed to have been a prophet mentioned in the Old Testament book of Jeremiah. He is identified as 'the priest Ahikam, son of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe' (Jeremiah 29:1, 3). Uziel is also referred to as 'the Gadite' or 'the priest of Gad'. The time period of Uziel's prophetic activity is not explicitly stated, but it is suggested that it occurred during the Babylonian captivity of Judah, around the 6th century BCE.

Another interpretation of Uziel's name is that it means 'my strength is God'. This name is given to a son of King Hezekiah mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in the New Testament book of Matthew (Matthew 1:8). The time period of Uziel's life during the monarchy of Judah is approximately the 8th century BCE.
